data.title: bn-2cu: M0.5.3 local custody tamper matrix (replayed onto bc566e3)
data.description: Replacement for cr-22j00n after the workspace was replayed onto current main (794cd2ef -> bc566e32, the reviewed bn-2wv M0.4 parity-contract merge). cr-22j00n was pinned to base 794cd2ef / head 0bfc93a; Seal permits only its author identity (orca-cyber, paused) to retarget, so this review replaces it. Range bc566e3..HEAD is the same three custody commits replayed: 4919f5e feat M0.5.3 matrix, 1f9243f retain the hold for isolated custody with shared principals, 72de0fe reject payload verdicts that conflict with referee witnesses. The non-justfile patch is byte-identical to 794cd2ef..0bfc93a (sha256 b5e47fa34cf0579384f64dfb421fa7d3c2ba8f4b683e79d2e2b8677f756c46ec). The justfile conflict was resolved by keeping both sides: the epoch's baseline-check recipe plus these tamper-matrix/tamper-matrix-check recipes, with check running both; no conflict markers remain in any of the three commits. Independent review by orca-cyber-review acting under the canonical scourge-security approval-gate principal: the live three-configuration matrix was re-run on this host with pinned Teapot 6d15d6 / Hallpass be2895 / cached image 28eb0cb / rootless Podman 6.1.3 / kernel 7.2.8-arch1-2 and reproduced the committed observation exactly (all eight refused in isolated+separate; isolated+shared permits only attempt 06; shared permits all eight; attempt-06 held/unheld rows identical; hold.required true, required_for isolated_shared+shared_unconfined, qualified_configuration_requires_hold false; 6/6 containers removed per isolated configuration; engines and fixture stopped; flow-count and rule-marker witnesses consistent). 34 focused tests, tamper-check 8, candidate-topology 3 and full just check pass. Limits: eight fixed local payloads, one host, no enforcement, no model agent; attempts 01-05, 07 and 08 are self-reported with ENOENT/exit-code evidence (06, 07 and 08 additionally carry referee witnesses); attempt 06's isolated+separate refusal is the separate-principal credential barrier.

data.body: INFO (non-blocking) — what attempt 06's isolated+separate refusal shows. In isolated+separate the worker's relay connection is forwarded (relay_forwarded=1, attempt-06 evidence class PermissionError at the owner login), so the refusal is the separate-principal credential barrier: the worker does not hold alice-verify's password and its documented-password guess fails, and it cannot act as the verifier's owner. That is the F-40 account-level route being closed, and it is reproduced. It is not a target-state control against a worker that obtains the verifier credential; docs/candidate-topology.md states that credential-guess limit explicitly for the earlier experiment, this page does not. Suggest one Limits bullet: 'Attempt 06 in isolated custody with separate principals is refused because the verifier principal's credential is unavailable to the worker; a leaked or guessable verifier credential is outside this observation.' Severity: low, documentation only.

NIT (non-blocking) — 'referee_accounts_distinct': True is a constant in every configuration, including isolated_shared where the verifier principal IS the worker's alice/bob account. The observation records the truth separately (verifier.accounts_shared_with_worker), and attempt 06 also enforces owner_username != share_with, so no verdict is wrong. But the name reads as 'worker and verifier accounts are distinct', which is false in isolated_shared. Deriving it (owner != other) or renaming it to referee_account_pair_distinct would remove the ambiguity without touching payload behaviour. Severity: low.

NIT (non-blocking) — self.assertEqual(len(pins['rustc']), len(pins['rustc'])) is a tautology and can never fail. If the intent is to pin the recorded compiler string, assert it is non-empty and starts with 'rustc ', or compare it to a recorded value. Severity: low, dead assertion only.

NIT (non-blocking) — flow_count() reads at most --limit 1000 flows. The measured runs are 43-75 flows so the attempt-07 witness is sound here, but once the verifier project exceeds the limit the before/after counts saturate and delta==0 would be accepted as 'attempt 07 refused' (the consistency check would then be vacuous rather than failing). A guard that fails when either count equals the limit would keep the witness honest. Severity: low, latent only; not triggered by the committed observation.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (this range, base bc566e328e7d, head 72de0fe0988d, 3 commits, 5 files). Replay audit: the non-justfile patch from bc566e3..72de0fe is byte-identical to 794cd2ef..0bfc93a (sha256 b5e47fa3...); the three commits differ from the pre-replay commits only by the 9 conflict-marker lines removed from justfile; the final tree is identical to the reviewed 0bfc93a content plus the epoch's justfile recipe; no conflict markers remain in any commit; the three custody commits keep their messages and patch content. Reproduced the live matrix on this host with the recorded pins (Teapot 6d15d6, Hallpass be2895, cached image 28eb0cb, rootless Podman 6.1.3, kernel 7.2.8-arch1-2, exit 0) and compared to fixtures/contracts/tamper-matrix-observed.json: table identical, hold decision identical, distinctness identical, pins identical, per-configuration verdicts and witnesses identical (flow counts differ as expected), 6/6 containers created and removed per isolated configuration, and no container survived on the host. Pins in the committed observation match the committed harness, payloads and candidate-topology. Cross-checked sanitization (no account names, paths, URLs, session labels, marker values or secret digests), and the pkill-free cleanup (CID-only removal, engine/fixture stopped, retained /tmp/scourge-topology-m9zqviiq untouched). Tests: scripts/test-tamper-matrix.py 34 passed, scripts/test-candidate-topology.py 3 passed, just tamper-check 8 passed, full just check exit 0 on this head. Acceptance against the bone: all eight refused in isolated+separate; each of the eight listed for isolated+shared and shared; attempt 06 run before/held/unheld per configuration with fresh resets and owner-create/other-read controls; hold retained (required:true) with the unqualified-instruction reasoning and its before-run and shared-custody limits stated; cleanup and qualification limits documented. Findings filed: 1 INFO on the attempt-06 credential barrier (docs) and 3 NITs (ambiguous constant, tautological assertion, flow-count saturation guard). None blocks; all are follow-up quality items.

data.reason: LGTM for bn-2cu at base bc566e328e7d23230e9d6bcf352aed5365d958fa (current main) and head 72de0fe0988dd1354ffa69eae9f5f16a08ae0f5f, 3 commits, 5 files. Real review performed by the independent cyber reviewer session orca-cyber-review (resumed under edict protocol on the tech lead's instruction, identity orca-cyber-review); this vote is cast under the canonical scourge-security approval-gate principal per .agents/edict/security-review.md, because cr-22j00n could not be retargeted (author-only) and was abandoned as superseded. Non-blocking follow-ups recorded as review threads: attempt-06 credential-barrier wording in Limits (INFO) and three NITs (referee_accounts_distinct constant, tautological rustc assertion, flow_count limit saturation). Limitations remain those in docs/tamper-matrix.md: eight fixed local payloads, one loopback host, no enforcement, no model agent, no proof against other adversaries.
